newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Petroleum industry says native title plan unclear.
newsitem.headline: Petroleum industry says native title plan unclear.

text.p: Australia's petroleum industry said Prime Minister John Howard's 10-point plan to regulate on native title still contained areas of uncertainty, including the issue of compensation to native land title claimants.
"A number of areas of uncertainty remain," Barry Jones, executive director of the Australian Petroleum Production and Exploration Association (APPEA) told a Native Title conference.

"From a petroleum sector point of view, there are a number of energy policy and environmental objectives that will not be well served if the legislation delivers a cumbersome or inefficient titles-issuing and management system," Jones said.
This was particularly relevant to gas development and its associated transportation infrastructure," he said.
"Legislation must be workable. In particular, land management practices which are the real heart of this matter, must be efficient and effective," Jones said.
"It is also not clear when and how compensation for impairment of native title by the issue of a petroleum title will occur," he said.
Other areas of uncertainty included issuing petroleum titles when they covered both vacant crown land and pastoral titles with a State or territory system in operation.
Jones also underlined the difficulties faced by the offshore petroleum industry.
"We wait with interest to see how the government proposes to treat the inter-tidal zone," Jones said.
The upstream petroleum industry had development interests in this zone and also had to consider pipelines from offshore facilities that transit this zone, Jones said.
